===== CORE DIRECTIVE =====
Rebuild the Bloom Cycle page instead of restyling the existing page.
Treat the supplied reference screenshot as the primary visual direction.
Treat the existing React application as the source of truth for real data, calculations, routes, persistence, and functionality.
Do not copy the current Cycle layout.
Do not copy the Profile layout.
Do not make a generic wellness dashboard.
Do not solve this by changing only colors, fonts, borders, or shadows.
Open the reference image and the current Cycle route side by side before coding.
Identify the major compositional differences before implementation.
Use the reference to determine hierarchy, proportions, density, spacing, visualization scale, and visual rhythm.
Make the browser implementation visibly different from the current screenshots.
If the final result could be described as the old Cycle page with prettier cards, consider the work failed and redesign the composition.
===== EXACT VISUAL TARGET =====
Build a dedicated Cycle Intelligence experience.
Use a deep near-black navy background.
Use restrained Bloom lavender and blue accents.
Use soft rose for menstrual information.
Use soft green for follicular information.
Use warm gold for ovulation information.
Use lavender-violet for luteal information.
Keep the phase colors consistent throughout the page.
Use an editorial serif for major headings.
Use a clean sans-serif for controls and metrics.
Use small technical labels sparingly.
Use thin borders and subtle surface contrast.
Do not put every section inside a bordered card.
Do not create a wall of identical cards.
Do not use huge empty spaces as decoration.
Do not use random glowing blobs.
Do not use excessive gradients.
Make the result calm, premium, sophisticated, and information-rich.
===== HERO REBUILD =====
Make the current cycle state the first visual priority.
Create a strong two-part hero composition rather than the current centered empty composition.
Use the cycle visualization as one of the largest visual elements on the screen.
Place contextual cycle information close to the visualization.
Show the current cycle day prominently.
Show the current phase prominently.
Show the cycle length when available.
Show whether the state is logged or estimated.
Show concise contextual copy.
Do not use a long marketing paragraph.
Do not leave a giant empty region between the heading and the useful information.
Create a clear primary action such as Log today.
Keep secondary actions visually quieter.
===== CYCLE WHEEL =====
Create a purpose-built responsive SVG cycle wheel.
Do not use a default chart-library donut.
Divide the wheel into proportional menstrual, follicular, ovulation, and luteal segments.
Calculate the segment proportions from the actual cycle model.
Place the current-day marker at the correct position.
Place the current cycle day in the center.
Show total cycle length beneath the center value.
Use subtle separation between phase arcs.
Use a refined outer ring.
Make the current-day marker visually obvious without a giant glow.
Keep the wheel optically centered.
Make the wheel responsive.
Make phase segments selectable.
Show a concise phase explanation when a segment is selected.
Provide a text alternative for accessibility.
Use softer treatment for estimated regions.
Never make estimated information look confirmed.
===== UPCOMING INTELLIGENCE =====
Place a strong upcoming-intelligence area beside the cycle wheel on desktop.
Do not make four identical statistic cards.
Give the most important upcoming event the strongest visual treatment.
Show the next period estimate when supported.
Show ovulation only when supported by the data model.
Show fertile-window information only when appropriate.
Show cycle-length information when enough personal history exists.
Show data sufficiency when it changes how the information should be interpreted.
Use varied visual hierarchy rather than identical boxes.
Allow important items to open deeper information.
Never fabricate prediction values.
===== NEXT SEVEN DAYS =====
Create a continuous seven-day timeline directly below the hero.
Do not make this another generic grid of cards.
Represent each day as part of the same visual journey.
Show date and phase.
Show relevant fertility or period state.
Highlight today clearly.
Distinguish logged from estimated days.
Allow a day to be selected.
Reveal selected-day information in a compact contextual area.
Allow the selected day to open logging details.
Use horizontal local scrolling on small screens if needed.
Never create page-level horizontal scrolling.
===== TODAY INSIGHT =====
Create a Today's Insight area based only on actual available Bloom data.
Do not generate generic AI text to fill empty space.
Use cycle phase, mood, energy, sleep, symptoms, and other supported signals only when available.
Explain why the insight exists.
Show the contributing signals in a compact way.
Use correlation language rather than medical causation language.
Allow the user to ask why an insight appeared.
Allow the user to dismiss irrelevant suggestions where appropriate.
Create a meaningful insufficient-data state.
Keep insight writing warm and concise.
===== QUICK LOG =====
Create a compact Log today action near the primary intelligence.
Do not put the entire advanced form in the first viewport.
Support the fields already supported by the existing application.
Allow fast logging of period or flow.
Allow fast logging of symptoms.
Allow fast logging of mood.
Allow fast logging of energy.
Allow fast logging of sleep.
Allow fast logging of temperature when supported.
Allow fast logging of cervical mucus or ovulation tests when supported.
Allow notes when supported.
Update the cycle wheel immediately after saving.
Update predictions after relevant logs.
Update insights after relevant logs.
Do not require a full page refresh.
===== HISTORY AND PATTERNS =====
Create a dedicated historical visualization using real completed cycles.
Show cycle-length variation clearly.
Show personal average only when enough data exists.
Show minimum and maximum when meaningful.
Make historical marks interactive.
Create a Your patterns section below the history.
Show recurring observations only when enough data supports them.
Show evidence such as observations across recent cycles.
Do not manufacture percentages.
Do not turn correlations into diagnoses.
Separate raw observation from interpretation.
Make the page become more personalized as more data is logged.
===== CALENDAR =====
Redesign the calendar as a secondary intelligence tool.
Do not reproduce the current oversized three-month grid.
Do not make every date a giant dark card.
Show one primary month at a time on mobile.
Show useful month context on desktop.
Mark logged period days.
Mark estimated period days.
Mark fertile estimates.
Mark estimated ovulation.
Mark today.
Allow date selection.
Show selected-date context.
Provide previous, next, and Today controls.
===== AI ASSISTANT =====
Add a floating Bloom AI control in the lower-right corner.
Make it feel like a native Bloom feature rather than a generic chatbot.
Use a subtle Bloom mark or spark icon.
Do not continuously animate it.
Open a compact assistant panel when clicked.
Give the assistant access only to context the user has permitted.
Let the assistant reference actual cycle data.
Let it explain observations.
Let it explain prediction uncertainty.
Let it suggest useful next actions.
Use contextual suggested prompts.
Examples include What should I pay attention to today, Why am I seeing this pattern, and What might the next few days look like.
Do not use generic chatbot prompts as the main suggestions.
Never invent a cycle value.
Never claim medical certainty.
===== PHASE EDUCATION =====
Create a visually refined phase education area lower on the page.
Give the active phase stronger visual emphasis.
Keep inactive phases quieter.
Explain each phase in simple language.
Separate general education from personal observations.
Use subtle abstract SVG forms if they improve the visual experience.
Do not turn phase education into four identical dashboard cards.
State that individual cycles vary.
===== DATA INTEGRITY =====
Never use the example dates from the screenshot as hardcoded production data.
Never use the example cycle day as hardcoded production data.
Never use the example cycle length as hardcoded production data.
Calculate every displayed prediction from actual application data.
Distinguish logged, calculated, estimated, and generalized information.
Handle zero completed cycles honestly.
Handle incomplete cycles honestly.
Handle missing optional fields gracefully.
Handle irregular cycles gracefully.
Do not display fake confidence percentages.
Do not describe incomplete data as healthy or normal.
===== REACT ARCHITECTURE =====
Implement this as reusable React components.
Separate data calculations from presentation.
Create components for CycleHero, CycleWheel, UpcomingIntelligence, CycleTimeline, QuickLog, CycleHistory, PatternInsights, CycleCalendar, AdvancedCycleLog, and BloomCycleAI.
Follow the existing project's architecture.
Reuse existing data services and state management where correct.
Do not rewrite unrelated routes.
Use responsive SVG for the wheel and visualizations.
Use CSS variables for design tokens.
Use semantic HTML.
Use accessible buttons and labels.
Do not hardcode chart geometry for one screen size.
===== RESPONSIVE =====
Support wide desktop screens.
Support laptop screens.
Support tablets.
Support mobile screens down to approximately 320 pixels.
Do not create page-level horizontal overflow.
On desktop use the strong two-part hero composition.
On smaller screens stack the composition intelligently.
Keep the cycle wheel prominent on mobile.
Move supporting intelligence beneath the wheel on narrow screens.
Make the seven-day timeline touch friendly.
Make charts resize naturally.
Prevent text clipping.
===== VISUAL QA =====
After implementation, open the actual /cycle route in the browser.
Take a screenshot of the browser result.
Compare it directly against the supplied reference image.
Do not judge success from code structure alone.
Correct composition before micro-styling.
Correct spacing before adding decorative effects.
Correct hierarchy before adding more cards.
Correct visualization scale before changing colors.
Perform at least three visual correction passes.
Pass one must fix overall composition.
Pass two must fix spacing, hierarchy, and density.
Pass three must fix typography, controls, icons, and micro-interactions.
===== IMAGE GENERATION =====
Generate a high-fidelity desktop concept before the final visual polish pass when image generation is available.
Generate the concept using the supplied reference image as the primary visual direction.
Generate a second desktop variation focused on the intelligence hierarchy.
Generate a mobile concept.
Generate a Bloom AI open-state concept.
Use the generated concepts as visual references for the React implementation.
Do not use generated images as excuses to add unsupported product functionality.
Compare the actual browser screenshot with the generated concept.
Iterate until the browser implementation has the same level of visual intentionality.
===== ANTI-GENERIC RULES =====
If all major sections have the same rectangular shape, redesign them.
If the hero looks like Profile, redesign it.
If the page has huge empty areas with little information, redesign it.
If the calendar is the main visual event, redesign the hierarchy.
If the cycle wheel looks like a generic donut chart, redesign it.
If the AI assistant only says How can I help, redesign it.
If the page looks like a generic period tracker, redesign it.
If the page looks like an admin dashboard, redesign it.
If the page is mostly borders and cards, redesign it.
If the visual reference and browser implementation have different hierarchy, follow the reference.
If a visual treatment conflicts with actual data, preserve data correctness and redesign the visual treatment.
===== FINAL EXPERIENCE =====
The first viewport must immediately explain the user's current cycle state.
The cycle wheel must be a dominant visual anchor.
Upcoming information must be easy to scan.
The next seven days must feel like a visual continuation of the cycle.
Quick logging must be close to the information it affects.
Personal history must become richer as data accumulates.
AI must be contextual rather than generic.
Calendar must support exploration rather than dominate the page.
Every empty state must be honest and useful.
Every prediction must communicate uncertainty appropriately.
The page must feel calm, premium, personal, intelligent, and unmistakably Bloom.
Do not stop when the page technically works.
Continue until the rendered browser result is visually convincing.
